{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1958)}}
[[File:AlexanderMielke.jpg|thumb|Alexander Mielke ]]
'''Alexander Mielke''' (born 14 September 1958.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Mielke CV |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/EC/2011-2014/CV-IMU-Mielke.pdf |website=International Mathematical Union }}</ref>) is a German [[mathematician]] working in the areas of [[nonlinear partial differential equations]] and applied [[mathematical analysis|analysis]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://mathplus.de/news/mathplus-distinguished-fellow-alexander-mielke/|title=Alexander Mielke|publisher=Berlin Mathematics Research Center|date=2024-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.wias-berlin.de/people/mielke/cv_mielke.jsp|title=Alexander Mielke short CV|publisher= Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics|access-date=2024-06-03}}</ref> He is a professor of applied analysis at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] and heads the research group on partial differential equations at the [[Weierstrass Institute]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.wias-berlin.de/people/mielke/|title=Alexander Mielke|publisher= Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics|access-date=2024-06-03}}</ref>

==Education and Career==
Mielke received his PhD from the [[University of Stuttgart]] in 1984 under the supervision of Klaus Kirchgässner, and his thesis was titled ''Stationary Solutions of the Euler Equation in Channels of Variable Depth''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Mielke |url=https://mathplus.de/news/mathplus-distinguished-fellow-alexander-mielke/ |website=mathplus.de |publisher=Berlin Mathematics Research center |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Mielke |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=27957 |website=Math genealogy |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref> He was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Cornell University]] under the supervision of [[Philip Holmes]] between 1986 and 1987, and in 1990, he [[habilitated]] at the University of Stuttgart on the topic of ''Hamiltonian and Lagrangian flows on center manifolds with applications to elliptic variational problems'' and was appointed professor at the [[University of Hannover]] in 1992.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.wias-berlin.de/people/mielke/cv_mielke.jsp|title=Alexander Mielke short CV|publisher= Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics|access-date=2024-06-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Mielke |url=https://mathplus.de/news/mathplus-distinguished-fellow-alexander-mielke/ |website=mathplus.de |publisher=Berlin Mathematics Research center |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref> In 1999, he was appointed at the Institute for Analysis, Dynamics, and Modeling at the University of Stuttgart. He has been a full professor at the Humboldt University of Berlin since 2004 and Head of the Research Group ''Partial differential equations'' at the [[Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics]] in Berlin.

===Awards and honours===
* [[Richard von Mises Prize]] of the [[Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik|Society of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics (GAMM)]], 1989.<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard-von-Mises laureates |url=https://www.gamm.org/en/info/foundation-prizes/richard-von-mises-prize/ |website=GAMM (Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik) |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref>
* [[Heinz Maier-Leibnitz-Preis]] awarded by the [[German Research Foundation]], 1989.<ref>{{cite web |title=List of all Heinz Maier Leibnitz Prize winners |url=https://www.dfg.de/resource/blob/170462/8abd602db7a5dbec2e6db6feecd31ef4/uebersicht-leibnitz-preistraeger-data.pdf |website=German research foundation (DFG) |publisher=DFG |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref>
* [[ISIMM]] Senior prize, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=ISIMM Senior prize 2024 winner |url=https://isimm.net/ISIMM-Prizes-2024/ |website=International Society for the Interaction of Mechanics and Mathematics}}</ref>
